clue.text: Episode on artist's compelling work

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an episode in someone's life or history can be called a page
J. M. W. Turner, the English painter; the possessive links him to the work

explanation.surface: A gallery-goer describes an artist's gripping painting of a particular episode.
explanation.walkthrough: TURNER is the English landscape painter, a crossword favourite for 'artist'.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a book so gripping that readers keep going, so it is a compelling piece of writing.

clue.text: Good-looking guy, notice, is following on

indicators.note: is comes after on, so it is placed following it

parts.note: an advertisement is a notice, shortened to ad

explanation.surface: Someone points out that a handsome man is tagging along behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name is used for any very handsome man.

clue.text: Where one may find a koala in difficulties?

definitions.text: Where one may find a koala
definitions.meaning: koalas live in eucalyptus, or gum, trees, so one may be found up one
being ... is a British idiom for being in a predicament

explanation.surface: A koala stuck somewhere awkward, needing help.
explanation.definitionFit: Koalas feed in eucalyptus trees, called gum trees, and the idiom means being stuck in a tricky situation.

clue.text: Wear son out in harbour

indicators.note: the son is taken out, so his letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to sport an item of clothing is to wear it

explanation.surface: Someone tells a son to wear something when going out around the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' tells you to remove S (son) from SPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A port is a town or place with a harbour where ships load and unload.

clue.text: Party member in protest about informer

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or rally
C stands for circa, Latin for about
a rat is someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: A politician is caught up in a protest against a police informer.
explanation.walkthrough: C is short for circa, about.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat belongs to the US Democratic Party, so is a member of a political party.

clue.text: Offer made by US soldier on foot

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
FT is the abbreviation for foot as a measure

explanation.surface: An American soldier on foot makes someone an offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is something given or presented, which is what an offering is.

clue.text: One after the other having an altercation

definitions.meaning: things ... follow one another in sequence
a row (rhymes with cow) is a quarrel

explanation.surface: People queuing in a line start arguing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads ROW as the British word for a noisy argument, rhyming with 'cow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Events in a row come consecutively, and a row is also a quarrel, so people in a row are arguing.

clue.text: Comic astounded, in camp in resort

indicators.note: to re-sort the letters is to arrange them in a new order

explanation.surface: A comedian is amazed to find themselves at a holiday camp in a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the holiday place but is the anagram signal: re-sort the letters of ASTOUNDED, IN and CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up comedian performs jokes alone on stage, and a comic is such an entertainer.

clue.text: I rushed round after second cocktail

indicators.note: I and what follows come after the second
the word is turned round, so read backwards

parts.note: to race is to rush, so raced means rushed

explanation.surface: Someone dashes round for a second cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reads as dashing about but is the reversal signal on the word for rushed, giving DECAR; 'after' puts I and that behind S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Expected of the French close to Nice

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Something French is expected to arrive near Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'near' but means the last letter of Nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something due is expected or scheduled to happen, as a train due at noon.

clue.text: Near end of shift, drink for hotel employee

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: As a work shift nears its end, someone has a drink with a hotel worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A night porter staffs a hotel's front desk overnight, so is one of its workers.

clue.text: Young reporters covering large nightspots

indicators.note: the young reporters cover, so go around, the letter for large

parts.note: cub reporters are young, inexperienced journalists
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Junior journalists are reporting on big night-time venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' reads as reporting on, but means the letters of CUBS wrap around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs are nightclubs, venues for dancing and drinking late at night.

clue.text: Move fast to expose what took place at Earls Court?

definitions.text: what took place at Earls Court?

parts.note: to motor is to travel quickly
to show something is to expose it to view

explanation.surface: Someone hurries along to reveal what happened at a London exhibition hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Earls Court is a former exhibition centre in west London that long hosted the British International Motor Show.
explanation.definitionFit: The British motor show, an exhibition of new cars, was held at Earls Court for many years.

clue.text: I clear that foul camp

indicators.note: something fouled is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone clears up a dirty campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' looks like a tent site but means flamboyant and exaggerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp behaviour is showy and exaggerated, which is what theatrical describes.

clue.text: In direct competition, make for cape

parts.note: to head to a place is to make for it
a head or headland is a cape on the coast

explanation.surface: Two rivals race each other towards a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-to-head contest pits two opponents directly against each other.

clue.text: Owner of large farm in France undressed, pursued by that woman

indicators.note: the woman's word chases, so comes after, the inner part of France
an undressed word has lost its outer layer, so its first and last letters go

parts.note: her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A wealthy farmer in France strips off and is chased by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher owns or runs a ranch, a large cattle farm.

clue.text: Is shy, awkward, before proper temper tantrum

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come before the word for proper
awkward letters sit wrongly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: fit means proper or suitable, as in fit for purpose

explanation.surface: A shy, awkward person has a proper tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A hissy fit is an informal phrase for a sudden childish outburst of bad temper.

clue.text: Competitor in event ran tactically

indicators.note: the answer sits inside these clue words, running across them

explanation.surface: An athlete in a race ran with clever tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who has entered a contest, so is a competitor.

clue.text: Apprentice in series, cheery at heart

parts.note: a train of events is a series of them

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A trainee in a run of jobs stays cheerful deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice learns a trade while working, so is a trainee.

clue.text: Feeling over in market, disordered place

indicators.note: the turned feeling goes inside the market

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: the word is turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: a sense is a feeling, as a sense of loss

explanation.surface: A sense of being overwhelmed in a messy market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the word for feeling to ESNES, and 'in' places it within the word for market; the answer is the idiom mare's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is an idiom for a chaotic, muddled situation or a messy place.

clue.text: MP and constituent

definitions.meaning: an MP is a ... of Parliament, often just called a ...
a component part, a constituent of a whole

explanation.surface: An MP and someone who lives in their constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituent' tempts as a voter in an MP's seat, but here means a component part.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament is a member, and a member is also a part or element of a larger whole.

clue.text: Spare not included

definitions.meaning: a spare one beyond the usual number
a cost marked ... is not included in the price

explanation.surface: A spare part costs more because it is not included.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is surplus or additional, and charges listed as extra are additional to the basic price.

clue.text: Employ engineer, mature

parts.note: to age is to mature, as wine does

explanation.surface: A firm hires an older, experienced engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone is to hire them, so it means take on as staff.

clue.text: Slightly drunk graduate, man giving good cheer

parts.note: merry is a mild word for tipsy
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
the king is a piece, or man, in chess

explanation.surface: A tipsy graduate is a man spreading festive cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: A chess piece is called a man, so 'man' can give KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrymaking is festive fun and celebration, which good cheer describes.

clue.text: Equipment heading for armoury in capital

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Military gear is carried at the front of an armoury in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia.

clue.text: Suffer mental anguish in hospital visiting one

indicators.note: the hospital letter visits, so sits inside, the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone goes through anguish while visiting a patient in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to feel pain, including emotional distress or longing.

clue.text: Composed of women, at that time lacking leader

indicators.note: the word loses its leading, so first, letter

parts.note: then means at that time

explanation.surface: An all-women group had no leader back then.
explanation.walkthrough: HEN describes all-female gatherings, as in a hen party, the British name for a bride's pre-wedding night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night or hen party is attended only by women, so hen here means all-female.

clue.text: Genuine gags, all funny, about hard subject to learn?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, so around, the letter for hard
funny letters are odd, so they are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Real jokes, all amusing, about a difficult topic to master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' looks like it describes the gags but signals the anagram, and 'about' wraps the result around the letter for hard. The question mark flags that the definition is a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: English is a school subject, and it is famously hard for foreigners to learn, hence the question mark.
